cells.tense: You are here, and the shapes are showing themselves before anything has settled into a question.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Go toward something that pulls at you before you've decided it should, and leave the pull unnamed for now. Notice afterward what you gave and what came back.
cells.core:
There's a way of reading a pattern that doesn't begin with the evidence — the shape lands, and it feels out a person or a room before you've decided anything. When it's clean it does one thing only: it lets an exchange go both ways. Today the shapes are arriving and you aren't forcing a verdict onto them. What you read, you read without holding back the next move.

So go toward something that pulls at you before you've decided it should, and leave the pull unnamed for now. Somebody will want your reasons before you've settled them yourself, and you can say you don't know yet. Notice afterward what you gave and what came back. What the two of you trade stays level; you don't have to justify your half first. Reading a shape and getting something back from it are the same motion here.
cells.sheetLine: You read the shape before you read the evidence.
cells.verb: opening before you know what you're opening to
cells.place: where the pattern shows itself with the content stripped away

cells.tense: By the time the moment arrives it will have been read already, and the person will be meeting your verdict.
cells.ask: Pick someone you've already decided about, hold that read for a week without adding to it, and ask one question whose answer you don't have.
cells.core:
You see where a situation is going, and you're usually right. Lately the reading finishes early: by the time a person sits down, a shape is waiting for them to fit into, and what they actually say gets checked against what you settled days before. The pattern gets a verdict while the moment is still forming.

Pick someone you've already decided about — you know the one — and hold that read for a week without adding to it. No new conclusions, no confirming details, no finished case. Ask one question whose answer you don't have, and sit with whatever comes back. It will feel like standing still while the ground moves under you. That's what an honest read costs; it can't close out what hasn't happened yet. What you ask, ask straight.

cells.tense: The pattern was there when it happened, and the reading stayed in the drawer while it went by.
cells.act: carry what the spark became to its full size
cells.ask: Next time a moment shows you what it means, say what you noticed before the subject changes. Four words is enough, said plainly.
cells.core:
Where the pattern shows itself, nothing reads it. Something lands at the table — a tone, a thing not being said, a shift in a room — and the moment passes without being looked at. You have the reading; it hasn't been out in a while. So the shape of what just happened gets assembled later, out of what other people say, and you end up repeating their version back to yourself.

Reading harder isn't the way back. One moment is. Next time a moment shows you what it means, say what you noticed before the subject changes — four words is enough, plainly. Don't build a case; just name it to whoever's there. What you saw reopens by being said once, and the next thing shows you more after that. Your own account comes back to you the same way.
cells.sheetLine: You have the reading. It stays in the drawer.

cells.tense: The read is happening under other names, and no one at the table says it belongs to you.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Give your read to the person it was about — what you saw, not what to do — and take back whatever they hand you in return.
cells.core:
You're reading something in someone, or in a room, and calling it a hunch, luck, the obvious thing. You saw it. Under that other name it does its work — you adjust, you hold back, you know before you're told — but nothing gets credited to the one who saw it, because the name you filed it under doesn't have a person on it.

Give your read to the person it was about. What you saw, not what to do about it, and take back whatever they hand you in return. You may learn you misread something; that's part of it, and the read is still usable. One exchange, running both ways. The reading doesn't stop being right once your name is on it — it only stops being invisible.
cells.sheetLine: You see it, and you file it under luck.
cells.verb: opening before you know what you're opening to
